# Device compatibility matrix

What the operating system supports for each device in the ZXV line: the
three consumer and three institutional briefcases, the six servers, and the
Signet, Folio and Courier handhelds. The specs live in `hardware/docs`; the
OS reads them as data from `kernel/src/devprof`. Everything below
"Summary by device" is generated by `make -C kernel device-matrix`, so
regenerate that part after any change to `devprof.c` instead of editing it.

Every "built" means tested in host tests or QEMU only. Nothing has run on a
physical board yet.

## Progress

Spec needs summed over all 17 devices (391):

| | Built | Partial | Missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before this work | 113 | 92 | 186 |
| Now | 195 | 104 | 92 |

Added: the device profiles and this matrix; board profiles for ZynqMP,
Versal and PolarFire SoC (each boots in QEMU) plus RK3588 (builds only,
since QEMU has no model); the arbiter mailbox with its PCI driver (attest,
key release, tamper, kill switches, seal, telemetry, start interlock); Opal
self-encrypting drive unlock over NVMe; an erasure-coded storage service;
thermal modes and the server climate controller, fed by arbiter telemetry
into the power budget; per-task route policy with satellite and LoRa link
classes; the DLP 1080p projector profile; igc and RTL8125 2.5 GbE drivers;
x86_64 machine-check and ECC reporting.

## Open questions for the owner

- **Pioneer arbiter.** OEM_CONSUMER.md says the Pioneer has no arbiter (an
  embedded controller instead). HARDENING.md and PORTS.md say every device
  has one. The profiles follow OEM_CONSUMER.
- **Pioneer quiet power.** 55 W in one place, 45 W in another; 45 W used.
- **Scram temperature.** 95 C and 88 C both appear; the climate profiles
  cite the section each value came from.
- **Micro-jet fault.** One section scrams on it, another limps home; it
  scrams (`jet_fault_scrams`).
- **Projector.** The spec says 1920x1080 native at 500 to 800 lm. No
  chipset is named; the DLP230NP default has a 960x540 mirror array shown
  as 1080p and is rated 450 lm.
- **Drive keys.** The arbiter's key slot is used directly as the Opal
  password; OEM_INSTITUTIONAL.md 6.3 says it wraps the drive secret. If
  wrapping is required, an unwrap step goes in `kernel/src/opal/opal_arb.c`.
- **Mesh compatibility.** Satellite and LoRa link classes are new; peers
  built before them reject capabilities from a device on those links.

## Remaining gaps and who holds them

| Gap | Holder |
|---|---|
| x86-smp, arm64-smp, x86-bigmem | Bare-metal OS thread (#133) |
| gpu-vulkan, gpu-cuda | GPU-first thread |
| wifi7, bt, acpi-aml, battery, touch | Hardware drivers thread (#140 for ACPI) |
| nic-10g, nic-25g, sas-hba, rk3588-soc, rk-vop2, hh-audio, radios (sat-ntn, iridium, uwb, gnss, sdr, LoRa radio, MBIM) | Driver backlog, for the build server once its runbook exists |
| nic-400g, amd-dcn | Need vendor firmware co-operation |
| boot-time attestation, pq-boot gate, SE051 seal signing, arbiter-fb compositor | Arbiter follow-up |
| answer-check, stripe-cluster | R&D in the specs (MOBILE_COMMON 3.4, SERVER_COMMON 8) |
| k3-board, camera-isp | Not started |
